Microbiota-Bile acid decoupling contributes to altered postnatal growth and metabolism in sFGR: a twin-paired dynamic study with FMT validation.

This study used monochorionic diamniotic twin pairs to show that selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) is associated with a decoupling between gut microbiota and bile acid metabolism, which may drive altered postnatal growth and metabolic outcomes. By combining metagenomics, 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomics, and fecal microbiota transplantation validation, the authors identify early-life microbiota-bile acid perturbations as a potential mechanism underlying sFGR-associated long-term health risks.

Fecal microbiota transplantation in cancer immunotherapy: targeting the Gut-Tumor Axis.

This review critically integrates clinical, ecological, and mechanistic evidence on fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as an adjunct to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) cancer therapy. It highlights that while FMT may enhance ICI efficacy and reduce intestinal toxicity, clinical responses are inconsistent and microbiome remodeling does not reliably predict benefit. The authors call for a more integrated understanding of the gut-tumor axis to guide future trial design and biomarker development.

Lung microbiota in COPD: a double-edged sword.

This review argues that the lung microbiota's role in COPD is a 'double-edged sword'—its effects depend on overall community structure and ecological balance rather than on individual beneficial or pathogenic taxa. The authors frame COPD as a model of disrupted respiratory ecosystem dynamics driven by immigration, elimination, local growth, and host-environment interactions.

Complete coding sequence of a virus belonging to the Chaphamavirus genus identified in a pooled blood sample from Actitis macularius birds collected on the Brazilian Amazon coast.

Researchers sequenced a complete viral coding sequence from a pooled blood sample of spotted sandpipers (Actitis macularius) on the Brazilian Amazon coast, identifying it as a member of the genus Chaphamavirus. The genome is substantially divergent from known chaphamaviruses, suggesting a distinct genetic lineage and possibly warranting taxonomic revision of the group. This adds a new geographic and host record for an understudied virus genus.

Multi-scale hybrid correction of noisy long reads.

DADEC is a new hybrid error-correction tool for noisy long reads that combines stringent de Bruijn graph correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive de Bruijn graph recovery in a confidence-ordered pipeline. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, it achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmarks while preserving genuine biological variation and avoiding over-correction.

Genome-resolved multi-omics characterizes bacterial, viral, and metabolic components associated with Parkinson's disease gut ecosystem variation.

This study combined deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing with fecal metabolomics in a high-altitude cohort of Parkinson's disease patients and matched spouse controls, reconstructing 455 species-level bacterial genome bins and 2,957 viral operational taxonomic units. The genome-resolved multi-omics approach links specific bacterial and viral taxa to metabolic features associated with PD gut ecosystem variation. It provides a high-resolution resource for understanding gut-brain axis components in PD.

Urban avian viromes reveal viral diversity of potential public health relevance across China.

This study performed a large-scale viromic survey of birds across 22 Chinese cities, identifying over 52,000 viral operational taxonomic units and revealing extensive previously underexplored viral diversity in urban avian communities. Viral richness varied markedly among cities, driven largely by bacteriophage diversity, while vertebrate-associated viruses were comparatively narrower in range. The findings highlight urban birds as a reservoir of viral diversity with potential public health relevance at the human-animal interface.

Aerobic and anaerobic cultivation shapes steroid-degrading wastewater consortia: Metagenomic insights into catabolic potential and antibiotic resistance genes.

This study enriched microbial consortia from dairy and municipal wastewater on the steroid hormones progesterone (P4) and 17β-estradiol (E2) under aerobic and anaerobic conditions, coupling degradation kinetics with shotgun metagenomics. Aerobic consortia removed >99% of P4 within 9–12 h and E2 within 24 h, far outperforming anaerobic cultures. Metagenomic analysis linked these differences to catabolic gene potential and revealed how cultivation conditions shape the carriage of antibiotic resistance genes in steroid-degrading communities.

The OMM12 model after ten years: what did we learn about the gut microbiome from a defined microbial community?

This review reflects on ten years of the OMM12 model, a defined community of twelve sequenced, culturable mouse-derived bacterial strains that simplifies the gut microbiome while retaining key ecological and functional features. It highlights how OMM12 enables reproducible, stable colonization across hosts and has been used to study colonization resistance and other mechanistic microbiome questions. The model is positioned as a cornerstone resource for controlled, mechanistic studies of gut microbial ecology.

Broad-spectrum in situ genetic reprogramming of native microbiomes.

This provides a powerful tool for studying and augmenting microbiome functions across ecosystems.
